summary: Fifth-order light on Old Gay Rock at the entrance to Wickford Harbor, first lit 1 November 1882; discontinued and demolished in 1930.

structures.note: Square wooden tower attached to a corner of an eight-room wood-frame dwelling (D'Entremont); 42 feet (13 m) from base to lantern (Archive). Discontinued and demolished 1930.
Small unmanned automatic light on a square skeleton tower, flashing green (D'Entremont; Archive 'Replaced by Skeletal Tower W/375mm Lens').

access.note: The U.S. Lighthouse Society Digital Archive lists the light as not open to the public.

events.note: Congress appropriated $45,000 on 15 June 1880 for a lighthouse on Old Gay Rock (D'Entremont).
Contractors began work on the lighthouse on Old Gay Rock (Narragansett Herald, 5 November 1881).
Square wooden tower and dwelling; Archive gives tower established 1882.
Fifth-order fixed white light first shown 1 November 1882; old Poplar Point light discontinued at the same time (D'Entremont; Lighthouse Board notice in the Weekly Visitor, 27 October 1882).
Fifth-order Fresnel lens (Archive: year original lens installed 1882).
Fog bell and striking machinery installed with the light (D'Entremont).
Keeper Edward (Edmund) Andrews recognized for the rescue of a drowning man (D'Entremont).
Keeper reprimanded for the subpar condition of the station; no action taken (D'Entremont).
D'Entremont: the lighthouse was destroyed in 1930.
Replaced as a cost-saving measure by a small unmanned automatic light (D'Entremont); Archive: replaced by skeletal tower with 375mm lens.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Archive gives 50 feet above water (15 m) and D'Entremont 52 feet (16 m) for the 1882 light. The record's 12.2 m (40 ft) figure has no source read for the 1882 light and is not used.
The record gives the 1882 wood tower as 4.5 m; the Archive gives 42 feet (12.8 m) from base to lantern, which is used here.
The record gives 1930 (Rowlett). The Archive gives year discontinued 1930 and disposition discontinued and demolished 1930, which agrees.
The record marks the station inactive. D'Entremont says a skeleton-tower automatic light flashes green on the site today, so the present light is active; the 1882 lighthouse is not.

The Archive roster and D'Entremont differ on Sherman (1882-1885 vs 1882-1886), Dodge (1885 vs 1886 start), and Andrews's length of service (1893-1930, thirty-seven years, vs forty years). The Archive's dates are used.

notes_for_editor: 1) D'Entremont is the only source for the 1880 appropriation, the 1878-79 Board recommendation (quoted from the Board's reports, which are not in the local corpus), the 52-foot height, the eight-room dwelling, the cistern, the fog bell, and all of Andrews's career detail. The Andrews family anecdotes (son's bicycle, children born on station) are used only as stated by D'Entremont and name no living person. D'Entremont's undated clipping anecdote about an 'essence addict' keeper and his daughters is NOT used: it is unsourced. 2) The Weekly Visitor notice is OCR'd ('November Ist, 1552'); the date 1 November 1882 is taken from the notice text and D'Entremont. 3) The Lighthouse Board repair lists (1896, 1897, 1899) name the station only in a list; the entries carry no detail. The 1897 list entry is OCR'd as '193. Wickford Harbor, R. I.' and was matched by its place in the FY1897 report (scan 316). 4) The Commissioner's $3,350 riprap figure is from an OCR table (Wickford Uarbor, R. 1 3,350). The 2026-10-28 fact-check read the archive.org page image at scan 378 (printed page 64) in the viewer: the Wickford Harbor row carries the figure on the same line, at the resolution the viewer gave. 5) The Wikipedia lead (not cited) gives 'a square wood tower attached to a 1 1/2-story keeper's dwelling' and 'Wickford Harbor Light 1'; not used because it conflicts with D'Entremont's eight-room house and is not confirmed. 6) The Archive's stated position (41 34.22 N, 71 26.14 W) is not corrected here. 7) The USCG Historian's page for Wickford could not be read (live site blocked; archived copies not used). 8) The record's 'inactive' status and the Fl G 6s characteristic describe the present automatic light rather than the 1882 light; see resolved_conflicts. 9) The Poplar Point Light (us-ri-poplar-point) and Whale Rock Light (us-ri-whale-rock) ids are from the data set; Sherman's Poplar Point stint and Andrews's Whale Rock service are cited only to D'Entremont. 10) Andrews's name: the Archive prints Edward; D'Entremont prints Edmund (often Edward); the roster name is used.
